input: The cost position has moved adversely since the previous forecast, and an overrun of 2 weeks is now reported against the current programme allowance. The underlying reason appears to be that rework followed a late change to the installed quantities, and once the installed work had been remeasured, the EPC forecast had to be revised to reflect the quantities actually in place rather than the quantities originally assumed. It is important to note that the overrun is not being attributed to a general loss of productivity across the project as a whole; the movement is concentrated in the packages affected by the change and by the remeasurement that followed it. In response, it is proposed that the remaining work packages be brought into a single re-plan, so that sequence, access, and float are considered together rather than package by package, and the project board is proposed as the owner of that re-plan. Such a re-plan would not undo the rework that has already taken place, but it would give the remaining work a single agreed basis, and it would prevent each package from continuing to plan against assumptions that the remeasurement has already overtaken. It is also the case that, until such a re-plan has been agreed, there is a risk that individual packages will continue to make their own local adjustments, with the result that the overall sequence becomes harder rather than easier to recover, and the movement reported here is better addressed while the remaining work is still capable of being reordered as a whole. The position, in short, is a defined movement against the allowance, arising from a specific change, with a single corrective action proposed in reply.
target: An overrun of 2 weeks is reported against the current programme allowance. Rework followed a late change to the installed quantities, and the EPC forecast was revised after remeasurement of the work in place; the forecast now rests on the quantities installed, not on the quantities originally assumed. The movement is concentrated in the packages affected by the change and the remeasurement. No general loss of productivity across the project is reported, and no part of the overrun is assigned to packages outside the changed work. The mitigation is a single re-plan of the remaining work packages. Sequence, access, and float are settled in the one re-plan rather than package by package, so no package continues to plan against assumptions the remeasurement has overtaken. The project board owns the re-plan. The re-plan does not undo the rework already done, and the overrun already reported is not recovered by replanning alone. What the re-plan changes is the basis of the remaining work: one sequence, one treatment of float, and one owner for departures from the agreed order. Departures after the re-plan are therefore visible as departures from a stated basis, rather than as further drift between packages working to different assumptions. The re-plan also fixes the order in which the affected packages are revisited, so the remeasurement is worked through in a sequence the site teams can staff, rather than arriving as separate demands from separate packages. Float is treated as a project resource in the re-plan: it is held where the remaining risk sits, and it is not left embedded in individual package programmes where it cannot be seen or moved. The reported position is a defined overrun with a named cause, and one mitigation with a named owner.
